s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic laryngeal infection with dysphonia and odynophagia in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Laryngoscopy showing thickening of the epiglottic mucosa with irregularity and white plaques
key_facts: Patient has a medical history of idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL)
Annual CD4 cell count ranges between 14 and 18 cells/µL
Initial presentation with a sore throat that did not improve after one week
Symptoms fluctuated in intensity over several months
No systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, myalgias) or pulmonary symptoms
Laryngoscopy revealed progression of white plaques
Laryngeal cultures grew multiple organisms including Candida albicans
Urine histoplasma antigen was positive at 0.3 ng/mL
Laryngeal biopsy revealed rare hyphae and yeast forms on Grocott methenamine silver stain
Fungal culture grew Histoplasma capsulatum

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic laryngeal infection with dysphonia and odynophagia in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Laryngoscopy showing thickening of the epiglottic mucosa with irregularity and white plaques
key_facts: Patient has a medical history of idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL)
Annual CD4 cell count ranges between 14 and 18 cells/µL
Initial presentation with a sore throat that did not improve after one week
Symptoms fluctuated in intensity over several months
No systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, myalgias) or pulmonary symptoms
Laryngoscopy revealed progression of white plaques
Laryngeal cultures grew multiple organisms including Candida albicans
Urine histoplasma antigen was positive at 0.3 ng/mL
Laryngeal biopsy revealed rare hyphae and yeast forms on Grocott methenamine silver stain
Fungal culture grew Histoplasma capsulatum

differentials: Squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx
Chronic laryngitis due to gastroesophageal reflux disease
per_call: Squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx
Chronic laryngitis due to gastroesophageal reflux disease

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Urine histoplasma antigen was positive and laryngeal biopsy revealed rare hyphae and yeast forms on Grocott methenamine silver stain

shortlist.label: Candidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Laryngeal cultures grew Candida albicans and patient has a history of immunocompromise

shortlist.label: Laryngeal tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of immunocompromise and chronic laryngeal infection

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Laryngeal biopsy revealed rare hyphae and yeast forms, which could be consistent with blastomycosis

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of immunocompromise and chronic laryngeal infection, making aspergillosis a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's urine histoplasma antigen was positive, and the laryngeal biopsy revealed rare hyphae and yeast forms on Grocott methenamine silver stain. Additionally, the fungal culture grew Histoplasma capsulatum, which strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Candidiasis
rejected.why: Although Candida albicans was present in the laryngeal cultures, the presence of Histoplasma capsulatum in the fungal culture and the positive urine histoplasma antigen suggest that Histoplasmosis is the more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Laryngeal tuberculosis
rejected.why: The acid-fast stain and culture were negative, which makes tuberculosis less likely.

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of Blastomyces dermatitidis in the cultures or biopsy results.

rejected.label: Aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of Aspergillus species in the cultures or biopsy results.
